parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State an experimental phenomenon that provides evidence for:

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: the particulate nature of electromagnetic radiation

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: A particle of matter moves with momentum $p$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the equation that gives the effective wavelength $\lambda$ of the particle. State the name of any other symbols used.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the name given to the wavelength of the moving particle.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Electrons are accelerated from rest through a potential difference (p.d.) of $4.8\text{kV}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Show that the final speed of the electrons is $4.1 \times 10^7\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the effective wavelength of a beam of electrons moving at the speed in $\text{(c)(i)}$.
